content.text:
This confirms it: before `adda54c14a`, `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` was set directly in the constructor right before the `getInteractionMode()` check. The commit `adda54c14a` removed that line and instead moved the assignment into a new `attachToProcess()` method called at the very end of the constructor — so the `getInteractionMode()` check that happens near the top of the constructor now always sees `consoleProcess_ == null`, incorrectly returning `INTERACTION_NEVER`. This exact line was restored by the bug-fix commit `cc2d5bb3f0`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: adda54c14a6158a684ee56e3b1dd1df94cdbe428

## Reasoning
(1) I examined the fix diff, which simply re-adds `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` right before the first `getInteractionMode()` check in the `ConsoleProgressDialog` constructor. I searched the file's git history (`git log --follow -p`) for all changes touching `consoleProcess_` and `getInteractionMode()` to find where this exact assignment at that exact location was removed.

(2) Commit `adda54c14a6158a684ee56e3b1dd1df94cdbe428` ("refactor ConsoleProgressDialog to support attaching to a process after construction", by Kevin Ushey, Feb 15 2017) removed the line `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` from directly before the `if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)` check in the constructor, and instead introduced a new `attachToProcess(ConsoleProcess)` method that sets `consoleProcess_` and is called at the very end of the constructor. It also changed the field from `private final ConsoleProcess consoleProcess_;` to `private ConsoleProcess consoleProcess_;` to allow this later assignment. As a result, when the constructor reaches the `getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER` check, `consoleProcess_` is still `null`, so `getInteractionMode()` always returns `INTERACTION_NEVER` regardless of the actual process's interaction mode — causing the dialog to always build a read-only output writer (`display_.setReadOnly(true)`) instead of an interactive `ShellInteractionManager` when it should be interactive.

(3) I verified via `git show adda54c14a^:...` that the pre-commit version had the assignment directly before the check (working correctly), and via `git show cc2d5bb3f0^:...` that the broken version (immediately before the fix) still had the assignment only inside `attachToProcess()`, called after the check. The fix commit's diff exactly reinstates the line removed by `adda54c14a`. No other commit between `adda54c14a` and `cc2d5bb3f0` reintroduced or touched this early assignment (confirmed by scanning all intervening commits' diffs to this file), so `adda54c14a` is the sole introducing commit.

I'm highly confident in this attribution given the exact textual match between the removed/restored line and its surrounding context.
